notes.text: Jose Alvarado is out and being evaluated, and Knicks coach Mike Brown gave no timeline: "I don't know how long." Tyler Kolek takes on more. "He can't let pressure bother him or disrupt our offense at all," Brown said. On defense, "he's got to be a pest."

Patrick Williams is still out for the Chicago Bulls and Tobe Awaka rolled his ankle "a little bit" today, Tiago Splitter said. Isaac Okoro sat the second half as Splitter went bigger with Zach Collins for "more emphasis on our paint, on rebounding the ball."

With Kawhi Leonard out, RJ Barrett thinks he'll get more of the ball for the Toronto Raptors and wants his drives to collapse defenses into open shots for teammates. Next: two games against Orlando, who he said are "down 2 starters right now."

Kawhi Leonard is out for Toronto. Darko Rajakovic: "when Kawhi is not playing, obviously that's missing a very important piece, but that opens up a lot of opportunities for other guys." Asked if Ja'Kobe Walter keeps starting, he wouldn't commit: it depends on matchups.

"It is good that it wasn't anything super, super severe. You know, give him some time and he'll be back with us." Orlando's Desmond Bane on Jalen Suggs's injury, a view Jase Richardson shared. Neither gave a timeline for his return.

With Jimmy Butler out and no timeline for his return, Golden State will play through Stephen Curry and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, Steve Kerr said: "We want to play through Steph. We want to play through Yax." He counted about 10 Lendeborg mistakes on tape.

Charles Bassey is "working his way back after being off for about 2 weeks," Draymond Green said, and he and Al Horford manned Golden State's center spot: "I'm comfortable playing a 5." Veterans must hold the fort so undrafted rookie Graham Ike can grow, he said.

Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg on his left foot: "now it's just tender... they said it should be nothing crazy." After a 3-point game in Hawaii, he asked Stephen Curry and Draymond Green for advice. They told him to be aggressive. "They pretty much just gave me free roam."

From Denver's media availability, on lost camp rhythm: "Cam being out, Spence having played a game." Cam: Cameron Johnson or Cam Whitmore, unspecified; Spence presumably Spencer Jones. DeMar DeRozan cited "a lot of injuries" and young players learning a defense new to him too.

Alex Caruso has an ankle sprain, and Thunder coach Mark Daigneault offered nothing more: "Ankle sprain. ... Nothing else." Missing key perimeter defenders, they started Kenrich Williams on Devin Booker, which Daigneault said "set an important tone."

With Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace out, Ajay Mitchell scored a career high for the Thunder: "I knew I'd probably have to come out and be even more aggressive." Isaiah Hartenstein said coaches must rework defenses without the pair's versatility.

"He finally seems like he figures it out, and then something fluke like this happens." Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on Thunder teammate Jalen Williams, hurt after "a tough year and a half with injuries." On the team getting whole again: "whenever that is, we don't know."

Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said tired legs are still affecting his jump shot: "just getting my legs back is the biggest thing... It'll take a couple weeks." After his first back-to-back, riding the bike mid-game, he's "a little beat up, but, uh, we'll be fine."

Alperen Sengun said he felt "a little pain in the game" after Houston's game but stressed he wasn't saying he got hurt: "I don't think about it." He says he feels healthy and at his best after a quiet summer (just two national team games in July) and a diet program.

Kevin Durant sat the whole fourth quarter at his own urging. "Kevin was like, let that unit roll," Houston's Ime Udoka said postgame. Fred VanVleet, Reed Sheppard, Tari Eason, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun "got stops, got out and ran." Udoka still wants his minutes down.
Asked why Aaron Nesmith played only 20 minutes, Rick Carlisle said: "He's got a 20-minute limit." The Pacers coach hedged on how long it lasts, saying only that it applied at least as of Oct. 26.

Sergio de Larrea left in the second quarter and gets imaging Oct. 27; no timeline. Mavericks coach Dusty May: "I don't know what it is... obviously concerned because he's such a tough kid." Walter Clayton Jr. stepped in after a stay-ready game earlier that day.

Anthony Davis was hit in the hand during the Wizards' game on Oct. 26, and coach Brian Keefe had "no update yet" on his status. Trae Young wants better spacing from Alex Sarr and others around Davis: "We just got to get into our spacing better when AD got us in iso."

Justin Champagnie is being evaluated for a right foot injury. Wizards coach Brian Keefe would not say whether X-rays were taken or came back negative. Trae Young spoke of Champagnie's "recovery": "We gonna make sure he's right and we'll hold down the fort while he's gone."

Steven Adams will miss "a week or two at least," Ime Udoka said before Houston's game; he felt something mid-game after earlier soreness. Clint Capela gets the first look at center, "but we're very comfortable going small." Marcus Smart is day-to-day, possibly back next game.

Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant Williams are "making positive steps in all their rehab plans," Charlotte coach Charles Lee said, some further along than others. No timeline yet. Their absence means a bigger role for Christian Anderson: "mistakes are going to happen."

Otega Oweh's roster spot had to be used, but the Thunder are still "really working closely with him on his rehab," GM Sam Presti said. Calling injuries "easily the worst part of the job," Presti said this group has a different identity and must find its strengths.

Yves Missi is still out for the Pelicans, with "no updates just as of yet," Jamahl Mosley said. DeAndre Jordan said he, Karlo Matkovic, Derik Queen and at times Zion Williamson will "hold down the fort until he's back," which has changed the rotations quite a bit.

Nick Nurse thinks four or five of the 76ers' power forwards and centers are out. Interior defense without Joel Embiid has "been a little bit of a concern"; Jabari Walker, Dean Wade, LeBron James and Adem Bona have all tried there. Of Bona: "the first game he's impacted."

"Played basketball my whole life. I want to feel normal." LaMelo Ball, asked if he must change anything to get through 5 games in 7 days for the Timberwolves. On Chris Finch leaving him in with four fouls early in the third quarter: "Yeah, for sure. That was love."

"I know we thin, so we all got to come in and rebound." With Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson out, the Detroit Pistons' Daniss Jenkins said after the Oct. 25 game that rebounding falls on everyone. He did his part with 8 rebounds.

Ivica Zubac's ankle X-rays were negative for a fracture, but it's swollen and Rick Carlisle called him "pretty unlikely" to play Oct. 26, "but we'll see." Ben Sheppard is unavailable and T.J. McConnell isn't back. Jay Huff and Larry Nance Jr. did "a terrific job" filling in.

Orlando's Paolo Banchero on his first career high ankle sprain: "I would say at least a month, you know, 4 weeks." He won't rush back so it doesn't linger. Anthony Black is questionable against the Knicks; coach Sean Sweeney didn't commit, saying it hinges on pregame shooting.

Back from tendonitis on a minutes cap, Golden State's Charles Bassey said he had no problems and could have played much more: "you guys should be expecting to see more of me." Steve Kerr said Georges Niang, out about a year injured, "doesn't have his legs underneath him yet."

Without their "main 2 guys," Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg, against San Antonio on Oct. 24, the Mavericks had "a lot of guys in positions to where they was uncomfortable, but that's, that's good for us," Daniel Gafford said, crediting the bench's resilience.

Bub Carrington was not injured when he left the Wizards' bench during their previous game, coach Brian Keefe said. Asked whether Carrington was sick, Keefe would not say: "was not injured. ... That's all I have for you."

Down Mark Williams and Oso Ighodaro, the Phoenix Suns are using Ryan Dunn and Miles Bridges at center sooner than planned. Coach Jordan Ott called rebounding the challenge when they go small. He didn't think Collin Gillespie grabbing his left hip was anything.

Asked if Luke Kennard is on a minutes restriction, Phoenix Suns coach Jordan Ott didn't confirm one: "He just hasn't played in a while. So we're going to be smart with that." Ott added: "every minute, every second he was on the court, we felt his impact."

VJ Edgecombe took ten 3s for the 76ers. Nick Nurse liked the "no hesitation" but said that volume won't come every night. His 13 rebounds came from crashing in, "a couple of games in a row," Nurse said. Dean Wade expects everyone "dog tired" Oct. 25 on the back-to-back.

Nate Ament made his NBA debut for Milwaukee after weeks out injured, crediting "the medical staff here and the team I got around me" for getting him back to 100%. He wanted to guard Jaylen Brown: "I wanted that challenge." On his early fouls, he's learning to be smarter.

With Oso Ighodaro out, the Phoenix Suns' Khaman Maluach said he and Duop Reath "both got to stand up for Oso" but he won't change his game: "It's not like, oh, Oso's out now, let me take a bunch of shots or bad shots, you know."

Tyronn Lue wants the Clippers to be smart with Brook Lopez's minutes, weighing them against what they ask of Isaiah Jackson: "he's 38, so, you know, we want to be smart." Lopez gave them a post threat and free throws off the bench against the Lakers.

From Golden State's media availability: Brandin Podziemski was relayed as saying he won't play Oct. 24. Yaxel Lendeborg "should absolutely be playing" in his first back-to-back and must be "way more aggressive" without Stephen Curry. Steve Kerr hasn't decided whether Curry rests.

Zach LaVine on Domantas Sabonis's return for the Sacramento Kings: "it was good to see him back and healthy," calling him the engine of their first half against Portland. Then: "The 3rd quarter is killing us." Portland was back in it within five minutes of halftime.

Deni Avdija played a lot of minutes out of necessity, Portland coach Micah Nori said postgame: "The good news is we have 3 days off for him to recover." A small lineup with Sidy Cissoko and Toumani Camara also kept Robert Williams III's minutes "down where we wanted them."

Domantas Sabonis is back from the first surgery of his career: "To be out for that long definitely was tough." Kings coach Doug Christie said they can "play through Domas in open sets and elbow sets," with Sabonis a second ball handler beside point guard Darius Acuff Jr.

Zach Edey is back from rehab, and Memphis Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo says "he's gotten more athletic" during it, crediting the medical and performance staff. Rookie Cam Boozer shows no sign of fatigue, Iisalo said, "so we got to be smart there."

"So thankful to be healthy," said Walker Kessler, who played 5 games last season and, 2 games into this one, joked he expects to pass that total. The Lakers center had 6 blocks and 3 steals but doubted the count: "I think they were pretty generous with the blocks."

Jake LaRavia was ruled out with an ankle injury after testing it at shootaround and in the treatment room. "It's not there," Lakers coach JJ Redick said. LaRavia, who played all 82 games last season and set doing it again as a goal, hopes to return Oct. 25, if not Oct. 27.

Oso Ighodaro has an oblique strain and is out for Phoenix's next game, but coach Jordan Ott said "we hope it's just more day-to-day than long-term." Luke Kennard practiced, "trending in the right direction." Khaman Maluach will "probably" see more possessions, Ott said.

Chet Holmgren and Jaylin Williams have moved to power forward, Holmgren said after Oklahoma City's Oct. 22 win: "we got other centers out there." He named Aday Mara, Isaiah Hartenstein and Thomas Sorber, the last "when he comes back." No timeline for Sorber.

Cam Johnson left Denver's game against Oklahoma City with ankle discomfort. Asked if it was minor, David Adelman didn't know: "I think Cam will be okay." Aaron Gordon's minutes are being held at a set level, which Adelman says makes it hard for Gordon to keep his rhythm.

Micah Nori praised how Damian Lillard came back in Portland's opener, and wants Toumani Camara and Sidy Cissoko taking the open 3s Lillard's gravity creates. Camara is "like 52%" on catch-and-shoot 3s in practice since Labor Day: "I don't think it's an aberration."

Kristaps Porzingis is not with the Warriors, and Stephen Curry said he hasn't spoken to him since training camp started. He called it hard on Porzingis and the team: "It is a tough one to figure out for the now, for the future... you would have loved to have him here."

Asked at Orlando Magic practice how his shoulder was feeling, Franz Wagner gave a one-word answer: "Good." Sean Sweeney on Anthony Black: "Full participant and working hard, shooting jumpers right now. Looks good and making them all."

"I'd be lying if I said there wouldn't be limitations. You know, there is pain there," Cleveland's Jarrett Allen said of tendinopathy in his knees that flared a few days ago as his workload ramped up. He plans to play Oct. 22 and doesn't think it will hold him back.

The Celtics' Mitchell Robinson says getting hurt "not really" affected him: "feel it a little bit here and there, but shit happens." On his last game: "obviously one of the best defensive bigs in the league and I didn't show it." He left Joe Mazzulla's last text unanswered.

Damian Lillard played his first game in 18 months in Portland's 2026-10-21 win over Phoenix, and Ja Morant called it the most mind-blowing thing of the day: "a guy hasn't played in 18 months and... he come out and... delivered the way he did for us. Special, man."

From Houston's postgame on Fred VanVleet's return: "he kind of calms the storm when it gets a little hectic." Amen Thompson is playing more off the ball, though Jabari Smith Jr. said: "He can play point guard, he can play in the dunker, he can play off the ball."

Without T.J. McConnell and Aaron Nesmith, Indiana is "mixing and matching with certain guys," Rick Carlisle said. From the postgame: the aim was to "keep one of our main point guards as the point guard the whole game," so Tyrese Haliburton and Jrue Holiday shared less time.

GG Jackson missed "over a week" of practice before the opener, and Tuomas Iisalo said it showed: the Grizzlies' bench of Jackson, Jerami Grant, Scotty Pippen Jr., Quinten Post and Cam Spencer got winded, "even the shorter subs, like 4 or 5 minutes."

Dejounte Murray on adjusting his shoe around his toe in the first half of the Pelicans' loss to Indiana: "Just readjusting my shoe. That's it. I'm good. Trust me, I'm good." He played 34 minutes after one preseason game, 12 straight once Jeremiah Fears hit foul trouble.

Adou Thiero has swelling in his knee, Lakers coach JJ Redick said on Oct. 21: "He'll be shut down for a couple of days and then... he'll ramp back up." The knee will need monitoring, he said. No timeline on Cameron Carr's oblique strain: "He's ramping up day to day."

Anthony Black is "getting close," Orlando Magic coach Sean Sweeney said at shootaround. "He's ramping up," but there's no return date. Until then Sweeney says he trusts the fill-ins, and Jamal Cain says he and Tristan da Silva have "been working, we ready."

Spencer Jones is "full go" for the Nuggets' opener, David Adelman said, minutes pending trainers. Christian Braun, hurt all offseason, probably feels freest since last year's Clippers game. Aaron Gordon is healthy: "When Aaron plays, we're as good as any team in the league."

"I have a few things that I know he doesn't really like, so I'm going to try to apply them. Can't tell y'all what it is though." — Bennedict Mathurin, facing Tyrese Haliburton for the first time in his Pelicans debut against Indiana. Haliburton is back and "healthy," he said.

"I basically didn't play for a whole year," Jalen Williams said after the Thunder's opener, but he expects a "pretty quick adjustment" and called his defense already great. Jared McCain, also back from injury: "When I was injured, it was just like the worst time ever."

Ben Simmons is out with no timeline, so Doug Christie changed his rotation plan. The Kings won't ask Malik Monk or Nique Clifford alone to replace his playmaking: "it's not going to be one person." Dylan Cardwell and Maxime Raynaud weren't with the team; everyone else is active.

"Everyone full, fully available," Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins said ahead of Game 1. Parting with Kevin Porter Jr. was "a very difficult decision," to open pathways for young guards. Brayden Burries gets early on-ball chances; he and Kasparas Jakucionis must grow as playmakers.

Precious Achiuwa, ready for the Sacramento Kings' season after "sitting out for a long time," says scoring isn't his job: "I don't really care offensively. It's just my job here is to make these guys better." Top priority: get Zach LaVine going early, and Darius Acuff Jr. too.

"Grateful... You got to be grateful through it all." Scoot Henderson on Portland not giving him a contract extension. He said the front office's message was that "they believe in me," and "right now I'm healthy, so that's as much as I can ask for."
Jase Richardson "made some shots, was moving pretty good" at Orlando's practice, Magic coach Sean Sweeney said: "He did a good job." Jonathan Isaac was out practicing as well, Sweeney said.

"It's just sad to see, 'cause you put in all that work to get back." Clippers coach Tyronn Lue on Ben Simmons, who he said had done the work and looked healthy. Asked about inactive Bradley Beal and Johnni Broome, he gave no statuses: "I think the guys are looking good."

Sam Merrill went through all of Cleveland's practice, scrimmaging included — "really good news," Kenny Atkinson said. Nae'Qwan Tomlin, who had earned a rotation spot, is out for a stretch with no return date; his spot goes to the "best player," not a like-for-like swap.

No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa rolled his ankle during preseason, Wizards guard Trae Young said, giving no status or timeline. Young raised it as a setback: "we fell short of that, obviously, with the number one pick AJ coming down, rolling his ankle."

Branden Carlson still has concussion headaches and isn't 100%, Portland coach Micah Nori said, adding Carlson has had one before: "So hopefully he will be okay." Chris Youngblood tweaked his Achilles but practiced a little. Micah Potter is still working back from an illness.

"Nate Bittle is out of the boot, so he's reconditioning now," Toronto's Darko Rajakovic said at practice, calling the team in "pretty good health." Asked whether Alijah Martin had tweaked his knee, he said Martin went through a whole practice and "was completely fine."

Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr missed Lakers practice again, JJ Redick said; Bronny James and Dalton Knecht had excused absences. Collin Sexton was "in practice, full participant," though Redick did not say whether he will play in the next game.

Asked for an update on Josh Hart, Knicks coach Mike Brown answered for the whole roster: "Yeah, no, no, everybody's healthy. Nobody was held out of any portion of practice." He did not address Hart individually.

Jalen Smith will start at center for the Bulls with Nic Claxton out, Tiago Splitter said, with Tobe Awaka "just coming back." Splitter wants everyone but the shooter chasing misses 75% of the time, up from about 40%: "we don't have the best shooting team in the NBA."

Cleveland's Kenny Atkinson said Nae'Qwan Tomlin sat out practice and Sam Merrill was limited; Khalifa Diop is "coming back from a setback." Atkinson wants a 10-man rotation, likely named only at game time: "I've made that mistake before... the guy tweaks an ankle."

T.J. McConnell (hamstring) isn't back yet and a couple more Pacers are still getting healthy, per Indiana's media availability. Quenton Jackson has run the bench at point guard; Rick Carlisle says he's "ready for... being a full-time roster guy and being ready at all times."

Joel Embiid is "ready to go" for the 76ers' opener, Nick Nurse said: "Some of those things weren't going on a year ago." Dean Wade, Dominick Barlow and Tacko Fall did not practice. Wade wore a practice jersey anyway. "Shouldn't make any judgments by those jerseys," Nurse said.

"I feel good. You know, just taking it day by day," said Anfernee Simons, who has missed 76ers practices over the past week. With no preseason game reps, he expects to "find my way" over the first 20 games. Asked if he'll play in the opener: "I can't confirm or deny that."

Max Christie was limited at Mavericks practice with a sore foot. "He's here shooting and doing stuff, but yeah, he wasn't full go," Dusty May said. Morez Johnson Jr. had a good practice, though May said "I can't imagine he's going to be able to play a full 48."

Orlando's Noah Penda will miss the start of the season with a new hamstring injury on the same leg as his first, which imaging showed had fully healed. Timeline? "I have no idea, honestly." He won't rush back. Sean Sweeney: whoever gains minutes has "to be ready to go."

"I feel great. I'm excited to play," a healthy Jalen Green said after the Suns' Oct. 16 game. He's slowing down from his Houston days as a table-setter, "not looking for my shot right away in the beginning of the offense," hunting the right pass and two feet in the paint.

Brandon Ingram is out of surgery. Tyronn Lue saw him when he woke: "He was in good spirits. And the doctor said it was a great surgery." No timeline; Lue says the Clippers can be special once he's back. With five rotation players out, young and two-way players get chances.

Kobe Sanders went through the Clippers' full practice on Oct. 17. Asked whether Sanders would be ready, Tyronn Lue gave no formal status but liked what he saw: "he looked pretty good. He's comfortable."

"Marvin hasn't played. He's been hurt." David Adelman explained why Marvin Bagley III got an extended fourth-quarter run in Denver's preseason finale. Tyus Jones got one too because "Tyus needed to play more minutes," and Adelman said he was very impressed with that group.

Ziaire Williams, back from a hamstring injury, was on a planned minutes limit and has foot soreness. JJ Redick hopes for "3 really good days with him" so the Lakers forward "can play more than 10 minutes" Oct. 21. Luka Doncic sitting the second half was planned, Redick said.
Khris Middleton is back playing for the Wizards. "Yeah, it's great to see him back out there," coach Brian Keefe said, calling Middleton a smart player who makes the right play.

Matisse Thybulle was set to start the Lakers' Oct. 16 preseason game, with a plan to play him 25 minutes "and see how he responds." JJ Redick said his workload will need managing all season. Quentin Grimes, who started the first four, will "start a lot of games," he said.

"Oh no, I'm playing." Asked at the Phoenix Suns' Oct. 16 shootaround whether he'd sit, Dillon Brooks said he'd play and named Jaren Jackson as his matchup. The gap before the opener in Portland, he said, is "a good little stretch to... get practice in and get healthy."

Oklahoma City came out of its Oct. 15 preseason game healthy, Mark Daigneault said. With Chet Holmgren and J-Will out, the Thunder tried a big-to-big action: "We've never worked on it. I don't know if you could tell." It showed what they'd need to work on if they explore it.

Wizards big Alex Sarr, back from injury, says he's "getting used to the pace" and has "been feeling good." Spacing beside Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton is his biggest adjustment. Brian Keefe wouldn't detail Khris Middleton's minutes: "he is trending in the right direction."

A left knee injury will send Julian Strawther for an MRI on Oct. 15. Nuggets coach David Adelman had no further information after Denver's preseason game on Oct. 14: "Hoping for the best, to be honest."

Davion Mitchell needed stitches near his eye in Miami's preseason game and stayed in. He shot his free throws, then got stitched: "this is just going to be a handful of stitches. I want to play." Erik Spoelstra said he still wanted the fourth quarter, and they let him.

"I definitely need one, one more game for sure." Giannis Antetokounmpo wants to play the Heat's final preseason game rather than sit it out, chasing as many reps as he can. Teammates and coaches want him to be aggressive and make plays, and he says he'll keep at it.

Keegan Murray played 19 minutes in the Kings' Oct. 13 preseason game, and Doug Christie said he is still finding his legs at both ends of the floor as Sacramento brings him back slowly: "19 minutes for him as we build him up is good."

Jamison Battle practiced and will be available Oct. 15, Raptors coach Darko Rajakovic said. Battle, Allen Graves and Kyle Anderson are in an open race for the 9th through 11th rotation spots, and Rajakovic said he is "not gonna shy away from throwing different guys in the fire."

De'Aaron Fox hasn't played a preseason game and Tobias Harris is "still coming back," with no timeline, Spurs' Harrison Barnes said at shootaround. Lineup undecided, so don't read it as an opening-night preview: "we're not gonna have our full roster until... a little bit."

Asked if he was limping, the Kings' Emanuel Sharp shrugged off the knocks: "So it ain't nothing new. ... But I'm good." Nor is he fazed by Damian Lillard, Ja Morant or Jrue Holiday: "I'm not looking at these guys intimidated or anything." He credits Doug Christie for that.

Max Strus, sidelined at Clippers practice, is "feeling a little better," Tyronn Lue said, "But we got to make sure we take our time." Brandon Ingram is doing more on the floor, but "it's going to be a while." Bradley Beal's knee rehab is "going pretty good," but no timetable.

Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins hopes Tyler Herro, out sick Oct. 13, is back Oct. 14. Nate Ament is moving more in the half court but still "constrained" — "positive progress," Jenkins said. AJ Green's knee, hurt against Minnesota, "feels good"; he's in knee pads and "good to go."

Anfernee Simons did half-court work at 76ers practice, no scrimmaging. On playing Oct. 16, Nick Nurse said "there's certainly some hope." He wants Simons back by Oct. 20, and Adem Bona too, "if we can." Healthy, Simons is his bench guard; if not, Labaron Philon Jr. plays.

"I think all 9 of us just seized the opportunity," Bennett Stirtz said of Oklahoma City's nine-man preseason roster, many with no G League or NBA experience. He played 37 minutes, hunting 3-pointers late with the paint packed; Mark Daigneault said pressure isn't new for him.

Jock Landale bled from the lip after a second-quarter play in the Hawks' Oct. 12 preseason game. "My lip's pretty sore right now," he said postgame, but called himself fine. He played past his usual 10 or so preseason minutes and said the extra time helped him find a rhythm.

Shaedon Sharpe is out and Micah Nori gave no timeline, saying Portland misses him "immensely." Nori still plans short stints across the roster, leaning on depth: "if we can keep them fresh, that's an advantage to us as other teams play their guys longer stretches."

De'Andre Hunter has played one game as a King and is still working off rust, Doug Christie said, but "DeAndre has been great." Christie likes him with Precious Achiuwa at center, Ben Simmons and Keegan Murray: "it's beautiful because you have the ability to switch."

Hornets' Tidjane Salaun, two preseason games in: "I feel pretty good with my body... I start to have a little bit more rhythm." His role is defense and rebounding: "that's where I can have the most success." Charles Lee says he's learning to impact offense without scoring.

Brandon Miller, back from a contusion and growing into Charlotte's number-one option, credited finding what he likes to do and that "the team trusts me to... go out there and perform the way I do." Since defenses won't help off him, they feed Naz Reid in the post often.

Every Knick came out of the last game okay and practiced, "a pretty good practice," Mike Brown said. Karl-Anthony Towns will pop out for jumpers a lot and has the green light to trail. Andre Drummond is told to keep rolling to the rim and shoot 3s only when wide open.

Dejounte Murray (toe) and AJ Johnson (finger) sat out Pelicans practice. On Murray, Jamahl Mosley said "we're just going to continue to be precautionary." On whether Murray could play through it once games count, he wouldn't commit: "We're 10 days into training camp."

Austin Reaves tweaked his ankle in training camp, delaying his first game next to Kevon Looney, the Lakers' media availability heard. Looney's role: screens that give Luka Doncic "easy looks where he don't gotta create for himself as much."

Ziaire Williams is "still dealing with that, like, kind of foot contusion. But again, it's not a concern," Lakers coach JJ Redick said Oct. 10. Arthur Kaluma is back: Redick said he returned to practice as a full participant.

James Harden "had a full practice," Kenny Atkinson said, "so assume he's going to play and start" in Cleveland's second preseason game. Atkinson thinks everybody is available, and the Cavaliers will "increase the minutes too for our main guys."

Jalen Suggs "did more" at Magic practice and "was looking more like himself," Sean Sweeney said; Nikola Vucevic expects him ready for the regular season. With Suggs and Anthony Black out, Jase Richardson and Jevon Carter play point; Sweeney liked Richardson's last game.

Matas Buzelis turned his ankle blocking a shot and left as a precaution; he expects to travel and hopes to play Oct. 11 in Denver, per Chicago's postgame. Tre Jones and Jaylin Sellers sat "out of abundance of caution." Down 5 rotation players, "it gets thin really quick."

Nuggets regulars should play again against Chicago, then Denver picks which of its two Los Angeles games to rest people, David Adelman said at practice. He'll take the injury risk with Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon since the group didn't play together last year.

De'Aaron Fox was a late Spurs scratch with "some tightness." Mitch Johnson doesn't "foresee it being anything serious" but will be "very cautious," and didn't say whether Fox travels to Phoenix. David Jones Garcia looks healthy after his ankle injury, Johnson said.

Anthony Edwards, back from an injury at the end of last postseason, hasn't looked limited. From Minnesota's postgame: "I haven't really noticed anything that he hasn't been able to do or anywhere he's been particularly cautious."

Jayson Tatum says he is healthy after 16 months with his injury, a year after "not knowing when or if I was going to... be back on the court." The Celtics star admitted: "Maybe I took the start of the season for granted. I just always assumed I would be out there."
